item.text: {"verdict":"request_changes","summary":"Two blocking portability/transactionality defects and three important concurrency/permission gaps remain.","recommendations":[{"severity":"blocking","location":"Architecture: container as boundary; Security battery, item 2","issue":"[P1] The mount invariant is internally contradictory. Docker implements `/etc/hosts`, `/etc/hostname`, and `/etc/resolv.conf` as daemon-generated host-backed bind mounts, yet the battery permits those files and then requires that no bind mount have a host source other than the credential directory. A literal implementation will reject every normal Docker container.","suggestion":"Distinguish user-requested binds from exact runtime-generated binds. Allow the generated files only at enumerated destinations with runtime-qualified source classes and options, while requiring the runtime configuration's sole user bind to be the credential directory. Update the broader “no host bind-mounts” claim accordingly."},{"severity":"blocking","location":"Installer & skill dispatch, steps 2 and 4–7","issue":"[P1] The proposed atomic upgrade cannot work as written: POSIX `rename` cannot replace an existing non-empty directory on Linux or macOS. The installed-byte check also occurs after the target becomes live, so an existing activation pointer can expose unverified bytes before the check or leave them active if it fails.","suggestion":"Install each bundle into a new immutable, versioned sibling directory; generate and validate release-scoped evidence there; re-hash it before exposure; then atomically replace a `current` symlink or equivalent pointer. Keep the previous release active throughout failures and switch both skill trees as one bundle."},{"severity":"important","location":"The credential — host-side broker; Testing strategy, item 5","issue":"[P2] The broker has no stated interprocess serialization or atomic refresh-token persistence protocol, and its test covers only sequential rounds. Concurrent installers, rounds, or battery controls can refresh with the same rotating token and then overwrite or invalidate the newly issued host credential, recreating the refresh race the broker is meant to eliminate.","suggestion":"Specify an OS-level interprocess lock around credential read, refresh, validation, and persistence; persist rotated credentials using an fsync-backed atomic replacement and generation check; and add concurrent-refresh tests, including one provider response that rotates the refresh token."},{"severity":"important","location":"The credential — staging mechanism; Container run configuration","issue":"[P2] “Owner-only” host permissions are not reconciled with the image's non-root UID/GID. On Linux bind mounts preserve numeric ownership, so a staging directory owned by host UID 1001 with mode 0700 is unreadable to a fixed image UID 1000; an unprivileged installer generally cannot chown it. Saying the mount has a defined UID/GID does not define a portable mechanism, especially across Docker Desktop.","suggestion":"Define and test the exact Linux and macOS ownership strategy—for example, run an arbitrary-UID-compatible image as the invoking host UID/GID and set tmpfs ownership accordingly, or use a protected runtime-managed volume populated by a constrained helper. Preserve owner-only host access and include the effective mapping in inspection and profile checks."},{"severity":"important","location":"Crash-safe bounding; Credential staging lifecycle; Testing strategy, item 6","issue":"[P2] The stale-directory reclamation rule is race-prone. An active runner can create its staging directory before creating the labeled container; a concurrent startup then observes no live container reference and may delete that active directory. “No live container references it” is necessary but not sufficient evidence that the directory is stale.","suggestion":"Hold a per-run lease or file lock from before staging creation through cleanup, and let the reaper delete only after it acquires that lease non-blockingly and confirms no matching live container exists. Correlate directories and containers with an unguessable protected run ID, and add a concurrent-start/reaper test."}]}
